verdict.line: You lose if Sett all-ins you between levels 2 and 6 before Wither is up to peel him; you win if you survive to Trinity Force and Frozen Heart and start landing Fury of the Sands in extended fights.

brief.thesis: Sett's Q (Knuckle Down) is on a 9-5s cooldown and buffs his next two attacks with bonus max-health damage, so he can poke-trade you constantly while your Q (Siphoning Strike) is on an 8s cooldown at rank 1 with no slow or burst to answer. The 50.4% head-to-head winrate over 1869 games matches your overall 50.4% Nasus winrate, meaning the early lane deficit is real but you claw it back once Wither and Spirit Fire come online and your late-game items let Fury of the Sands out-scale his all-in kit.

theirWindow.what: Sett's Knuckle Down (9s cooldown at rank 1) empowers his next two autos with max-health damage, so he can walk up and trade freely. Don't auto-trade back; just last-hit with Q and give up contested CS.

yourWindow.what: Wither (700 range, 15s cooldown at rank 1) decelerates his Movement and Attack Speed over time. Throw it the moment he engages with Knuckle Down's move speed buff so his punches land slower and he can't walk you down.

powerCurve.note: No slow yet, his Q wins every trade
Facebreaker plus level 6 ult threaten all-ins
Wither and Spirit Fire offset his grit sustain
Trinity Force and Fury of the Sands out-scale him

start.why: Run in 62.7% of games at a 49.3% winrate; the passive block and regen directly counters Sett's auto-reliant poke and the health regen he gets from his own passive when low.

boots.why: Picked in 41.7% of games at 50.1%; Sett's damage comes from basic attacks and Knuckle Down's empowered autos, so flat attack-speed-scaling damage reduction blunts his entire trade pattern.

core.why: The highest-performing path (55.9% over 313 games) when followed by Frozen Heart and Spirit Visage; the damage spike lets you threaten trades once Wither is landed.
Attack speed slow punishes Sett's auto-reliant kit and his passive left/right punch alternation, while the armor blunts his physical burst.
Heal and shield power amplification stacks with your Soul Eater lifesteal in extended trades and sustains you through his poke.

situational.when: he builds lifesteal or crit to lean on his passive sustain and empowered autos
he's snowballed an early kill and you need cheap armor fast to survive ganks
you want the poke and waveclear path over Trinity Force's burst (48.6% over 70 games)

runes.keystoneWhy: The move speed and healing on movement let you kite Sett's Knuckle Down engages and Facebreaker range while still farming safely, which matters most since he wins straight stand-and-trade exchanges.

summoners.why: This combo has the highest measured winrate at 52.4%; Ghost lets you close distance to land Wither or disengage from his Knuckle Down speed boost, and Flash covers the level 6+ threat of The Show Stopper grabbing you.

playing.title: Last-hit, don't auto-trade
playing.detail: Your Q is on an 8s cooldown at rank 1, so use it purely for CS. Walking up to auto Sett just eats a Knuckle Down-empowered attack with bonus max-health damage.

playing.title: Save Wither for his engage
playing.detail: Hold Wither until he commits to a trade or all-in, then land it immediately. The ramping Movement and Attack Speed slow cuts his damage output and lets you walk away from the fight.

playing.title: Zone contested CS with Spirit Fire
playing.detail: Drop E on the spot he needs to stand to farm or trade. The armor reduction and persistent damage pair with Wither to flip extended skirmishes in your favor.

playing.title: Don't fear Facebreaker alone
playing.detail: In a pure 1v1, Facebreaker only stuns if he has enemies on both sides of him; with just you in lane it will slow instead of stun unless a jungler gank puts a second body nearby.

playing.title: Watch his Grit bar before trading
playing.detail: Sett stores all damage he takes as Grit for Haymaker's shield-and-punch combo. If he's been tanking poke and his Grit looks full, back off rather than starting a fight into his shield.

playing.title: Respect level 6 all-in range
playing.detail: The Show Stopper has a 400 range and carries you into the air to slam you. Don't push past the minion wave right as he hits 6 until Wither is ready to slow his follow-up.

playing.title: Flip late fights with your ultimate
playing.detail: Once Trinity Force and Frozen Heart are online, force fights near a wave so Fury of the Sands' max-health drain and bonus range let you out-trade his tankier, all-in playstyle.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and the 50.4% head-to-head winrate over 1869 games are measured OP.GG data from the current patch; the mechanical reasoning, trade patterns, and timing calls are my own read of how the two kits interact.
